# FormattingRouteParitySweepTests ratchet (P22e, issue 2168).
# One row per failing (stem, twin, route, state, bucket):  stem twin route state bucket # #issue
# A row covers every cell of that route and state on that stem and twin. A row whose (route, state) ran
# and now holds, or has no cell, fails the sweep: delete it (drain on fix). Populated from a FULL-mode run
# (SHARPY_ROUTE_SWEEP_FULL=1, the FMTROUTE-ROW lines of the test output). cli and full rows on S1/S2 are
# refused by the loader. Phases 2-3 of P22e drained this file to empty; P22f (issue 2271) re-populated it with the
# S5/S6 cells its Phase 2 drained and the S6n/S6k cells of their own trackers. P22g Phase 1 (plan-d923d3) replaced
# the 20 S6k rows with a pinned census count (KnownLimitPin, issue 2274, R-FQ) and re-populated it with the S6n
# rows of the four budget-stop positions (issue 2273) and the S6r rows (issue 2275) its Phases 2-3 drain. Phase 2
# drained the 334 S6n rows: the editor's indent map lexes past the error budget (R-FP). Phase 3 drained the 240 S6r
# rows: a re-paired closer is recorded for any abort on its line whose given-up text holds a quote (R-FR). Empty.
# P22h Phase 1 (plan-f92797) re-populated it from a FULL-mode run with the S7 depth rows (issue 2279) and the S6o
# factSpurious rows (issue 2280) its Phases 2-3 drain.
# Buckets (T = the applied text, D = the document):
#   edits        the edit list is not legal for D (the strict applier threw)
#   net          CheckMeaningPreserved(D, ast(D), T) refuses T: the applied text changes the program
#   whole        cli/full/range-whole: T differs from Format(D) (full modulo line breaks; CRLF and CR kept on range-whole)
#   local        range kinds: T is neither D nor D with the selection's hunks applied
#   fixedPoint   S1: a route edits a document that is already Format's fixed point
#   ontypeShape  ontype: T differs from D other than in the requested line's leading whitespace
# Unparseable documents (S3 cut after a block opener, S4 cut inside a multi-line literal, S5 an unmatched
# triple quote inserted as line 0), ground truth from the parent twin's clean lex:
#   content      a line is lost or gained, or changed beyond its leading whitespace, or its line break changed
#   literal      a line that starts inside a literal is not identical
#   depth        a logical line's block depth in T (the lexer's width rule) differs from its depth in the parent
# The S6 family (P22f, P22g) loses a literal WITHOUT a lexer abort inside its read, every document derived from Q by
# FormatterTwins.LiteralLossShapes; the label (FormattingRouteParitySweepTests.LossState) fixes the cite:
#   S6    the budget spent above a Q holding a multi-line literal (at any of FormatterTwins.BudgetStopLines), a stray
#         triple re-paired into a short string, a delimiter line dropped at SPY0011-SPY0015 or SPY0004 (a short
#         string aborting mid-line) — cite issue 2271 (closed: no S6 row may be added; a failure is a finding)
#   S6n   the budget spent above a Q holding NO multi-line literal (the cure's direction control)   — cite issue 2273
#   S6k   the stray triple re-paired into a comment (a known limit of any lexer fact)               — cite issue 2274
#         its literal-bucket cells are a pinned census count (KnownLimitPin), never rows
#   S6r   the short-string re-pair whose orphan line aborts right after the closer (repair-SPY00NN) — cite issue 2275
#   S6x   a closer line that aborts and drops no quote, no stray (closeline-SPY00NN): nothing is lost, the direction
#         control of issue 2275 — cite issue 2275; any S6x row is a finding, never a row
#   S6o   the own-quote close-line tails (P22h): closeline-own-NAME, a closer line whose tail aborts inside a literal
#         of its own (no stray: nothing is lost, its rows are factSpurious), and repair-own-NAME, the same tail after a
#         re-paired closer followed by the orphan's closing quote (a literal IS lost: a factMissing row there is a
#         finding, never a row) — cite issue 2280
# S7 (P22h, FormatterTwins.ContinuationShapes) injects a line as the first body line of the parent's first block: an
# unclosed bracket (bracket-eof, bracket-string, bracket-backtick, bracket-dropped) or an erroring line (recovery, and
# recovery-misindented with the line after it 2 spaces deeper); judged by depth against the parent's layout, its line
# routes on the line after the injection (recovery-misindented's skip the wide twin) — cite issue 2279; S7 loses no
# literal, so an S7 factSpurious or factMissing row is a finding, never a row
# On every unparseable document (S3-S7; not S6k), the lexer's literal-loss fact itself:
#   factMissing  Lexer.LiteralStateUnknown is false while a line that starts inside a literal in Q does not in D
#   factSpurious Lexer.LiteralStateUnknown is true while no such line is lost (never a row on S6n or S6x: a finding)
# The reason after an S-family cite lists the shapes whose documents fail the bucket.
